hard_rules: FOLDERS (owner, 25 October: two chats at once must not get in each other's way). This chat works ONLY in cores/continuum-gb/** for B1 to B5. B6 to B8 (the phone's camera, two Game Boys on one screen, the Advance link between phones) are the only items allowed to change the app or the engine (native/**, crates/**); they come last on purpose. cBoy's own code only: cores/continuum-gb/**. App or engine changes that an item needs (camera, two screens) are allowed, and must keep every other core working; run the engine tests too.
Another chat may be working on the GameCube core at the same time: never touch cores/continuum-gc/**, and pull before every push (git pull --rebase).

Never guess a test picture pixel by pixel: follow how a proven emulator models it, and compare against it.
Run the whole cBoy suite before every push (cd cores/continuum-gb && scripts/fetch-test-roms.sh && cargo test --release). Never weaken a test.
Every look or behaviour change gets a setting with a sensible default (owner: everything is customisable).

items.title: Game Boy Advance timing: the cartridge prefetch buffer and exact wait states
items.notes: Today a simple prefetch model. Measure with the jsmolka/AGS-style timing tests and mGBA's suite (mgba-suite) before and after; some demanding games depend on it.
items.result: Done 25 October (commits c7e2bb1, 7061656). Measured with Alyosha's timing tests (alyosha-tas/gba-tests, MIT, 133 ROMs written against a real console; mGBA's suite needs devkitARM, which this sandbox cannot download). Before: 47 of 133 (prefetch 1 of 18). After: 64 of 133, all 18 prefetch-buffer tests and both prefetch on/off tests; pinned in tests/gba.rs alyosha_timing_tests, fetched by scripts/fetch-test-roms.sh. What changed: the Advance CPU has its real two-opcode pipeline (each instruction's read at r15, jumps refill N then S); every access is sequential or not as the CPU says (N after any data or internal cycle); the prefetch buffer is modelled halfword by halfword the way the tests' author's own emulator (GBAHawk) does it; DMA: first unit N, rest S, internal cycles split before/after, an immediate DMA starts 2 cycles after its write and overlaps the CPU's internal cycles; the work RAM wait register ($04000800); timers on the shared prescaler with the real start delay (and the FFFF-on-enable overflow); registers read/written at the end of the access; ARM jumps keep bit 1. Reference used: GBAHawk (Alyosha's emulator) built locally in .scratch only, with a stand-in BIOS, as a cycle-by-cycle comparison (it passes 102 of 133 that way); nothing of it is in the repo. Older Advance save states still load (the new timing state is appended after the fixed layout). Speed: about 5% slower than before on the six homebrew games here. Not done (not prefetch or wait states): a DMA interrupted by a higher-priority one, interrupt entry delay, the serial port's timing, sprite fetch timing, BIOS-dependent start-up tests.

items.title: Sound accuracy: SameSuite's APU tests
items.notes: STATUS: SameSuite's APU tests mostly fail; normal game sound is fine. Follow SameBoy's APU model.
items.result: Done 25 October. cBoy's sound chip rewritten to run at its own 2 MHz clock the way SameBoy models it (behaviour followed, code written from scratch): countdowns that reload a tick late, trigger delays, envelope clocks that lock, zombie-mode volume nudges, the sweep's delayed recalculation and its NR10 glitches, the noise channel's 14-bit counter and its NR43 write glitches, the DIV event on the falling edge and the envelope set-up on the rising edge, wave memory access while playing, revision E of the Color (the Game Boy's own differences where known; the Advance's PSG uses it too). SameSuite's 70 sound tests: 9 -> 57. SameBoy itself, built here from source and run on the same files, passes exactly the same 57 and fails the other 13 with byte-identical results (7 are for other revisions, 6 SameBoy also gets wrong). Blargg's dmg_sound and cgb_sound: 17 -> 24 of 24. Both pinned in tests/roms.rs (blargg_sound, samesuite_sound); scripts/fetch-test-roms.sh fetches Blargg's and builds SameSuite with rgbds. Older save states still load (the chip is saved after the fixed layout; an old state's channels carry over). Speed: within a few percent of before.

items.title: Two Game Boys on one phone (dual console, linked by cable)
items.notes: Gaps: sameboy_screen_layout, sameboy_audio_output, tgbdual_* (5), savePlayerId. Two machines in one core, both screens drawn side by side or one above the other, which one is heard, swap.
items.result: cores/continuum-gb/src/dual.rs: two Game Boys run the same cartridge in step (real time, 64-dot slices), joined by the link cable (the driving console's byte reaches the other as its eighth bit goes, the answer comes straight back). Settings in Link: Two Game Boys on this phone (next start), where the screens go (one above the other / side by side, next start), screens shown (both / first only / second only), swap the screens, sound (first / second / both), your controls play (first / second: the on-screen buttons and first controller play it, a second controller the other). The second keeps its own battery save, '<game> (second Game Boy).sav' in the app's save folder, written every 2 s when changed and at exit. Save states hold both. No app or engine change needed: the app sizes the picture from what the core reports and passes a second controller as player 2. Tests: dual.rs unit tests, options_e2e two_game_boys_on_one_phone (a byte crosses each way, screens, swap, controls, single screen, the save file) and two_game_boys_change_shape_only_at_the_next_start. Not done: two different games (the app opens one file), infrared.

items.title: Game Boy Advance link: cable multiplayer and the wireless adapter
items.notes: Gap gpsp_serial. The Game Boy/Color cable between two phones exists (Built, untested; link.rs). Owner said yes to the wireless adapter (25 October).
items.result: Cable done: cores/continuum-gb/src/gba/sio.rs. Normal 8/32-bit and multi-player (16-bit) modes go to a second phone through the app's existing two-phone session (same netpacket interface as the Game Boy cable, own protocol name cboy-advance-link-1, own 7-byte packets). The hosting phone is the parent. The driving console's transfer stays busy until the other phone answers, gives up after 6 frames reading all 1s; with no second phone a transfer finishes on its own reading all 1s (before, the busy bit stuck for ever). Tests: sio.rs unit tests, link_e2e an_advance_word_crosses_to_the_other_phone_and_back and an_advance_on_its_own_reads_nobody. NOT done: the wireless adapter (a large command protocol that only real games such as Pokemon FireRed/Emerald could check, and none are here); UART and JOY Bus modes; more than two players. Wireless adapter added 25 October evening (owner said yes): cores/continuum-gb/src/gba/rfu.rs. The NINTENDO start-up exchange, the commands (hello, setup, broadcast, host, poll, broadcast read, connect, data send/receive/wait, disconnect, bye, status), the adapter-driven wait events and timeouts, the SI ready signal; the radio as messages over the same two-phone session. Setting Advance link port: Auto (an adapter for games that look for one, the default) / Link cable only. Test: tests/wireless.rs runs afska's LinkWireless demo (MIT) on two Advances, which find each other, connect and count both ways. Not checked: Pokemon FireRed/LeafGreen/Emerald (Nintendo's own library), which only the owner's phones can.

items.title: Start the Sega 8-bit core: Master System, Game Gear, SG-1000 (working name continuum-sms; owner: never ask about names, decide and note)
items.notes: Why this one is next: Continuum already has its own Z80 (cores/continuum-arcade/src/z80.rs) passing SingleStepTests' Z80 suite, ZEXDOC and ZEXALL. The rest: the VDP (TMS9918 modes plus Mode 4, Game Gear palette and window), the SN76489 sound chip, the YM2413 FM chip (Japanese Master System), the Sega, Codemasters and Korean mappers, the Game Gear start button and link, light phaser and paddle. The bar: Gearsystem (the app's current core) and Genesis Plus GX; settings = every setting Gearsystem, Genesis Plus GX, PicoDrive, SMS Plus GX and Emulicious offer, plus our own (do a settings inventory first, like cBoy's and the GameCube's). Tests: ZEXALL for the Z80 on the real memory map, the SMS VDP test ROMs (Flubba's VDPTEST, the SMS Test Suite), and real open-licence homebrew. Replaces Gearsystem (GPL v3) when it matches it.
items.progress: 25 October evening: name picked cGear (shown in the app; crate continuum-sms; change it here if wanted). Done, each with tests: settings inventory (docs/SMS_OPTIONS_INVENTORY.md); cArcade's Z80 compiled in from its file; Master System memory map, Sega, Codemasters and Korean mappers, cartridge RAM, memory control port; the picture chip: ports, registers, V counter, line and frame interrupts, mode 4 (background, scrolling, sprites, flags) and the TMS9918 modes (graphics I/II, text, multicolour, TMS sprites); the SN76489; the Game Gear (palette, 160x144 window, Start, ports, stereo); the SG-1000 (no banking, 1 KiB RAM, TMS9918 only); Pause as NMI; save states; 14 settings (options.rs; which inventory rows they cover is in the inventory); libretro entry points (sms|gg|sg|bin) with an end-to-end test. ZEXALL-SMS passes in full (tests/zexall.rs, 3 minutes). 26 October: the YM2413 FM chip is in (src/fm.rs; ports $F0/$F1/$F2, settings cgear_fm Auto/Off/On and cgear_fm_volume, so 16 settings; then FM channel 1-9 volumes, Soften the sound (low-pass), Game Gear whole picture and a Weak ghosting step, CPU speed, Colours in SG-1000 modes, Borders (the TV border from Charles MacDonald's VDP document), 3-D glasses games, Bass/Middle/Treble: 34 settings; 26 October: the Light Phaser, Paddle and Sports Pad (src/peripherals.rs; both ports, relative and absolute Sports Pad modes, Japanese and export paddle; phaser latches the H counter where it points on bright lines; crosshair drawn by cGear; aimed with the stick or D-pad, and by touch once the app sends touches for Master System games, which it does not yet): 43 settings; then the Korean MSX, Nemesis and Janggun wirings and Auto for region (default; header region code or file name) and refresh rate (file name); then the Game Gear link port and Gear-to-Gear cable (src/link.rs, MacDonald's GG I/O notes: pins $01/$02 with the cable's crossing and NMI on TH, serial $03-$05 with speeds and NMI on receipt) and two Game Gears on one phone (6 settings, the second's save '<game> (second Game Gear).sav' in the save folder): 49 settings. Then Console: Master System (first model) / Mark III, the 315-5124's differences (no tall picture, register 2 bit 0 name-table mask, zoom on the first four sprites only). FluBBa's VDPTest now passes in full, 55 of 55 (tests/vdptest.rs pinned): sprite overflow found on every picture line with the screen off too, collisions in the border, the collision flag when the beam reaches it, the frame flag and next line's overflow seen by a read that runs into the next line, the line interrupt one cycle into the line. Console start-up screen (cgear_bios: bios.sms / bios.gg from the system folder, the app's install list knows them; CoreSpec max size now 320x294 for two Game Gears and borders). 51 settings. SC-3000 (Console value sc; .sc files route to cGear in the app and detect.rs; the keyboard through its 8255, MacDonald's matrix, phone keys mapped in libretro.rs read_keyboard; 16 KiB cartridge RAM for BASIC). tests/homebrew.rs (HOMEBREW_DIR, games not committed): all 65 games of retrobrews/sms-games boot and draw for 30 s with no panic; their pictures looked right on a contact sheet (26 October). The Gear-to-Gear cable between two phones too: a Game Gear on its own offers the app's link (netpacket, protocol cgear-gg-link-1; packets [P, pins] and [S, byte]; tests/link_e2e.rs); checks: tables, pitch, attack/release, detection and mixing; not yet compared with a recording of the real chip, drums roughest). Next: the timing inside a line (see vdptest_25_october), the rest of the settings from the inventory (49 in; the inventory's done column says which rows they cover), the light phaser, paddle and sports pad, the Master System II / Mark III / Japanese differences (region, port $3F), the Game Gear link and two consoles on one phone, then build-core.sh and the app (an app change: needs the owner's go-ahead).
items.percent_25_october: About 35%: CPU, mappers, picture (mode 4 and TMS modes, not yet measured against the picture test ROMs), basic sound, Game Gear, SG-1000, states, 14 settings done; YM2413, 67 settings, light phaser/paddle/sports pad, region/console differences, the start-up file, Game Gear link, mid-line picture timing, test-suite measuring, real games and the app hookup left.
items.vdptest_25_october: FluBBa's SMS VDP test 1.31 (tests/vdptest.rs): data page 19 of 19 OK, misc page 14 of 16 after the H counter (the hardware's table, latched on TH) and port accesses at the end of their I/O cycle, sprite page 16 of 20; all pinned. The failures are the H counter (its value, its latch on TH, its mirrors), when inside a line the V counter changes and the interrupts and flags fire, off-screen-Y collision and overflow with the display off. Next for accuracy: a cycle position inside the line for every port access, then the H counter and those timings, then the X-scroll latch page.
